title: The National Archives UAP records collection (RG 615)
notes: The first entity-resolution case: five nodes that were one thing are now one (nara-rg615 and the records-collection twin collapsed in phase 4).

lead.text: Sections 1841 to 1843 of the FY2024 NDAA ordered a collection of government UAP records at the National Archives, which NARA holds as Record Group 615. It is what survived of the UAP Disclosure Act: the review board and the eminent domain provision were removed in conference.

summary.text: The statute puts records of technologies of unknown origin and non-human intelligence into federal law as categories the Archivist must collect, but leaves identification, transfer and postponement to the agencies that hold the records.
On the board's reading the collection descends from decades in which the only auditable finding was GAO's 1995 report that the Roswell base's records had been destroyed with no recorded authority.

NARA's first release, announced on 24 April 2025, came from ODNI, the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission; by 28 August 2026 eight agencies had series in the collection.
In 2026 two executive channels ran beside it: the Department of War's PURSUE releases and an ODNI memorandum directing all intelligence community UAP information to a PURSUE Task Force.
The House-adopted FY2027 amendment would add statutory transfer timelines and a Senate-confirmed review board with subpoena authority to the collection.

record.text: Public Law 118-31, approved 22 December 2023, enacted the UAP subtitle as sections 1841 to 1843, and NARA established Record Group 615 under them; records received from agencies are accessioned into it and published on a rolling basis.

The enacted sections correspond to sections 9004 to 9006 of the Senate-passed Division G; the Review Board, the eminent domain provision over recovered technologies and biological evidence, and the other Senate sections have no enacted counterpart.

The statute bars destruction or alteration of any UAP record, required each agency head to review and organise its UAP records for disclosure and transfer within 300 days of enactment, requires records to be open for inspection within 30 days of transmission and online within a further 180, and requires full disclosure within 25 years unless the President certifies harm.
Postponement is decided by the original classification authority on clear and convincing evidence of one of four harms; no independent board reviews it.
NARA issued transfer guidance to agencies in April 2025 and asked agencies with releasable records to begin transfers before 30 September 2025.

NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the NRC; CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA, NSA and DOE transferred nothing for it, although ODNI had named DIA, NRO, NGA and NSA among the contributors to its 2021 assessment.
By 28 August 2026 the Record Group 615 page listed eight contributors: the FAA, NRC, ODNI, OSD, NSA, the Department of State, the FBI and the Department of the Air Force, which was added that day.
The FAA series holds 575 PDF files and is restricted in part under the postponement code 1843(a)(3).

The Air Force series holds 30 items, 8,093 pages dated 1945 to 1969, scanned with no searchable text; one item carries an Air Force declassification block citing the FY24 NDAA and dated 5 May 2025, while a 1960 bomber wing history in the same series had been declassified in 1982.

Among the Air Force items is a Fourth Air Force file of 1947 UFO reports whose index records liaison with the FBI on flying-disc reports, correspondence about Kenneth Arnold, and a report on the Crisman and Dahl disc story.

ODNI memorandum ES 2026-00818, signed by Principal Deputy DNI Aaron Lukas and published by Rep. Eric Burlison on 1 August 2026, directs release of all UAP information to the PURSUE Task Force for review and declassification, waives prior NDAs, oaths and commitments when witnesses speak to AARO or PURSUE, and gives every intelligence element 30 days to name a PURSUE designee.
The memorandum's distribution runs to the directors of CIA, DIA, NGA, NRO, NSA and FBI, DOE's intelligence office and the intelligence chiefs of every military service.
NARA already held the Project Blue Book records, 94 rolls of microfilm, and states that none of them discusses Roswell.

The statute has NARA's National Security Program Office run, with the Information Security Oversight Office, a security programme for the postponed part of the collection; ISOO is itself a NARA component responsible for the classification system.
For comparison, Brazil's Air Force began sending its holdings to the Arquivo Nacional of its own motion, a fund of 743 records, while the US collection exists only because a statute ordered it.

claimed.text: The Department of War states that AARO has made progress in transferring UAP records to the National Archives in accordance with federal law, and AARO's records page links first to the collection.
Senator Gillibrand said of the Department of War's 8 May 2026 release that it was another important step and that she would keep fighting to make the administration meet its legal obligation.
Burlison said he was uncertain whether the abrogation of NDAs would apply to testimony received by Congress before referral to the executive branch.

The 1969 Bolender memorandum is quoted throughout the literature as saying that UFO reports affecting national security go through JANAP 146 or AFM 55-11 and are not part of the Blue Book system; the archived scan is an untranscribed image.

contested.text: The board infers that the absence of the intelligence agencies and military departments from the first transfer means either they hold no UAP records, which ODNI's 2021 contributor list contradicts, or they have not sent them; as of 28 August 2026 CIA, DIA, DOE, NASA, NRO, NGA, DHS, the Army and the Navy still had no series.

The agency review deadline fell about 300 days after enactment, in October 2024, while NARA's guidance is dated April 2025; the board infers the deadline was not met, and Gillibrand described the May 2026 release as the administration only beginning to meet its legal obligation.

The records disagree on what NARA publishes about compliance: an August 2026 reading found no list of transferring agencies, counts or dates, while the Record Group 615 page lists eight contributing agencies.

Accession into Record Group 615 is not evidence that a record had been withheld: the Air Force transfer mixes newly declassified pages with material declassified decades earlier, and the item catalogued as the 1948 Estimate of the Situation is a Far East theatre estimate, not the Air Materiel Command estimate Ruppelt described.
The board infers that no series matching the JANAP 146 national-security UFO reports or the Air Materiel Command T-2 files of 1947 to 1951 has been identified in the collection.
On the board's reading neither PURSUE nor the statutory collection can be audited, and the PURSUE Task Force has no public charter, roster, chair or budget line.
The page-header identifiers stamped on four Air Force items belong to other records, so page-level stamps in that series are not reliable for provenance.

questions: Which agencies have transferred UAP records, how much, and when, and why does NARA not publish that accounting?
Will CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA and DOE, all addressees of the ODNI memorandum, ever place a series in Record Group 615?
What has been postponed from the FAA series under code 1843(a)(3), and by whose determination?
Where are the JANAP 146 national-security UFO reports the Bolender memorandum is said to describe?
Who sits on the PURSUE Task Force, under what charter, and does its review feed the statutory collection?
Does the NDA waiver reach testimony given to Congress, and on what date was ES 2026-00818 signed?
